title: Chapter 46: Suspect
html:
As the details began to connect, Chen Ge’s expression tightened. Standing in the security office, he called Inspector Lee at the Western Jiujiang police station.

The phone rang twice before Inspector Lee’s gravelly voice answered. “Hello?”

“Uncle San Bao, I need to report something.”

“First, emergency reports go through 110. Second, my name is Inspector Lee.”

“I think I just saw the remaining Ping An Apartments fugitive at New Century Park.”

Inspector Lee’s tone changed immediately. “Are you sure?”

“Pretty sure. He has already left, though. I did not confront him.”

“Stay where you are. We’ll be there shortly.”

After the call ended, Chen Ge kept his eyes on the surveillance footage. The guards had realized the situation was serious and quickly contacted Uncle Xu.

“What happened now?” Uncle Xu hurried in with a water bottle in hand. “Can I not finish one lunch in peace? Xiao Chen, why are you here instead of at the Haunted House?”

He noticed the footage on the monitors, then the phone in Chen Ge’s hand. “Who did you call?”

“The police.” Chen Ge kept scanning the feeds. “They are on their way.”

“The police? Why did you not tell me first?” Uncle Xu’s voice rose. “Park management has procedures for theft, accidents, emergencies—”

“Uncle Xu.” Chen Ge turned to him, calm enough that the words sounded even more serious. “I think someone came here looking for me.”

The security room fell silent. Every guard turned toward him.

“Chen Ge, what exactly are you saying?” Uncle Xu stopped using his usual nickname, a sure sign that he was worried.

“I helped the police uncover the Ping An Apartments case, but one suspect is still at large.”

Understanding dawned on Uncle Xu. “You think the man on the footage is that suspect—and that he came here because of you?”

“That is my concern.” Chen Ge pointed to the monitor. “He keeps his face down, dresses in a way that hides identifying features, and behaves as though he is watching the area rather than enjoying the park. None of that proves anything by itself, but together it is suspicious.”

“Suspicious, yes, but not proof,” Uncle Xu said. Even so, he crossed the room and closed the security-office door.

“The fugitive’s name is Zhang Peng. His build matches, and he has a distinctive peony tattoo on the back of one hand.”

“A peony?”

“Yes. The case file mentioned it.”

“And you think that is why he kept one hand hidden?” Uncle Xu was beginning to take the theory seriously.

“There is more.” Chen Ge switched clips. “After entering the park, he rode only the Ferris wheel—and did it several times. Then he approached the Haunted House only when he thought Xiao Wan and I had both left.”

Uncle Xu frowned. “You think he was watching the place?”

“Exactly. Whatever his reason, he was not behaving like a normal visitor. He spent most of the morning observing the Haunted House from a distance and moved closer only when it seemed unattended.”

“That is enough to make me uncomfortable,” Uncle Xu admitted.

Chen Ge tapped the desk. “I do not know what he intended, and I am not going to pretend I do. But after Ping An Apartments, I would rather let the police decide than ignore the pattern.”

Uncle Xu’s expression hardened. “On that, we agree.”

“The worst part is that I almost dismissed him as just another visitor.” Chen Ge exhaled slowly. “If I had not recognized him, I might never have checked the cameras.”

“Where is he now? Do we need to warn everyone?”

“He left after he realized I had returned. At the time I was not certain enough to confront him, which was probably for the best.”

“Definitely for the best.” Uncle Xu turned to the guards. “When the police arrive, give them whatever footage they need.”

About ten minutes later, three plainclothes officers entered the security room. Inspector Lee led them. “Where is Chen Ge? Show me the footage.”

With help from the park staff, Inspector Lee compared the recording against police records. The identification was confirmed: the visitor was Zhang Peng.

“You did the right thing calling us.” Inspector Lee immediately contacted the investigating team. The officers began coordinating surveillance around the park and the surrounding area.

“Zhang Peng is considered dangerous,” Inspector Lee warned. “If he is targeting you, do not approach him. Let us handle it.”

The guards looked uneasy. Chen Ge was calmer than they expected. “If I suddenly disappear and close the Haunted House, he may realize we recognized him.”

Inspector Lee frowned. “You are not suggesting that you act as bait.”

“I am suggesting we keep things looking normal while the police decide what to do. I am not volunteering to chase him.”
